35: Heh (the letter). When it comes at the beginning of a word, it hints at Binah, and when it comes at the end of a word the hint is to Malkhut.
Hevel (“Vanity”). Seven “Vanities” are the seven [lower sefirotic] qualities.
Haggadah (“Recital”). From the side of Ḥokhmah.
Hadas (“Myrtle”). The three “patriarchs.” Malkhut [is called] Hadassah.10Hadassah was Esther’s name. Cf. Esther 2:7.
Hu (“He”). In Keter or in Binah or in Tiferet or in Malkhut.
Hod (“Majesty”). It is so called when it is held by Gevurah and Binah.
Havah (“To Exist”). Hints at the upper heh, the lower heh, and the vav in the middle.11This is a reference to the three sefirot, Gedulah, Gevurah, and Tiferet. Cf. sec. 6, chap. 5, n. 29 above.
Havi (“Existence”). Tiferet removes itself with the blessings to Binah.

Hallel (Psalms of Praise). Malkhut when it is not completed.12Hallel is a series of psalms of praise recited in the synagogue on various holidays. On some of them, not all the psalms are recited and the Hallel is considered “incomplete.” Completed [it refers] to the side of Binah or to Binah herself.
Halleluyah (“Praise the Lord”). Malkhut from the side of Tiferet.
Har (“Mountain”). Malkhut. All is in accordance with the [divine] Name which accompanies [it].
Hatkafah (“Attack”). Malkhut from the side of Ḥesed.
